title: Tibet mega-dam: the largest infrastructure project on earth, unmapped
thesis: China's Yarlung Tsangpo (Motuo) hydropower complex, launched July 2025 at a stated ~$167B scale, is a decade-long buildout with second-order chains in heavy construction, tunneling, HV transmission, and downstream water geopolitics (India/Bangladesh) that Western markets have barely priced anywhere.
why_now: Construction formally launched mid-2025; procurement and transmission-corridor decisions land over 2026-2028, exactly the window where suppliers get contracted before earnings show it.
retail_gap: Coverage treated it as a one-day China-politics headline. Almost no mapping of the supplier chain (tunnel boring, HV DC transmission, cement/steel logistics at altitude) or of the riparian-risk angle for Indian utilities and agriculture.

unmappedness.rationale: Event is known; its chain is essentially unmapped in Western coverage. Investability is the open question (largely Chinese SOEs), which is exactly what a chain build should establish.

evidence.claim: Groundbreaking of the Motuo hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo was announced by Premier Li Qiang, with reported investment around 1.2 trillion yuan (~$167B) and five cascade stations.
evidence.source_name: Reuters / Xinhua reporting on the July 2025 launch

evidence.claim: India publicly raised downstream-flow concerns; Arunachal/Assam riparian exposure is a live bilateral issue, creating a parallel Indian buffer-dam and monitoring response.
evidence.source_name: Indian government statements and press coverage post-announcement
